mainTopic: The כהן גדול's two chambers in the עזרה: the לשכת פרהדרין in the north and the לשכת בית אבטינס in the south, proven from the משנה in מדות that lists the six chambers of the עזרה.
overview: The גמרא explains that the כהן גדול was brought to בית אבטינס to practice חפינה, scooping a handful of קטורת. רב פפא says the כהן גדול had two chambers, the לשכת פרהדרין and the לשכת בית אבטינס, one in the north and one in the south. A משנה in מדות lists the six chambers of the עזרה, and אבא שאול places the כהן גדול's chamber on the northern side. A second משנה places שער המים in the south, and a ברייתא says the כהן גדול's first immersion was on top of שער המים, beside his chamber. Together these prove he also had a southern chamber. The גמרא does not know which named chamber was where. It suggests the לשכת פרהדרין was in the south, so that he would not have to walk back and forth so much. That reasoning is rejected: the extra effort is intentional, either to push out a צדוקי or to keep the כהן גדול humble, as the two separate chambers show. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the elders calling the כהן גדול 'our agent' refutes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who holds that כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא. His proof begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the כהן גדול was brought to בית אבטינס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the כהן גדול was taken to בית אבטינס to learn חפינה, the skill of scooping incense with his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A תנא taught: They brought him there to teach him how to take a handful of incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining a detail in our משנה: why the elders brought the כהן גדול to the House of אבטינס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול must scoop a double handful of קטורת. This is very hard to do exactly right, so he needed practice. בית אבטינס was the family that prepared the incense, so that was the natural place to train.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught; it introduces a ברייתא
Scooping a handful of incense with both hands
The family and chamber in charge of preparing the קטורת

phrases.english: Gemara:
A Tanna taught: to teach him the taking of handfuls.
phrases.notes: This tells us why the משנה has him brought to בית אבטינס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by clarifying the purpose behind an action in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול was brought to בית אבטינס in order to be trained in חפינה.

steps.title: The כהן גדול had two chambers, one north and one south
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the כהן גדול had two chambers: the לשכת פרהדרין and the לשכת בית אבטינס, one in the north and one in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The כהן גדול had two chambers. One was the פרהדרין chamber and one was the chamber of בית אבטינס. One was in the north and one was in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא teaches that the כהן גדול used two separate chambers during his preparation, located on opposite sides of the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה mentions both the לשכת פרהדרין, where he stayed for seven days, and בית אבטינס, where he trained. רב פפא tells us these are two different rooms on opposite sides of the courtyard. The גמרא will now try to prove where each one stood.

keyTerms.meaning: Chamber / chambers in the מקדש
The chamber where the כהן גדול stayed during the seven days before יום כיפור
North / south

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי לְשָׁכוֹת הָיוּ לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: The High Priest had two chambers,
one was the Parhedrin chamber
and one was the Chamber of the House of Avtinas.
One was in the north and one in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שְׁתֵּי לְשָׁכוֹת הָיוּ לוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of בית אבטינס by mapping out the כהן גדול's two chambers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול had two chambers, the פרהדרין and בית אבטינס, one in the north and one in the south.

steps.title: Proof for the northern chamber: the six chambers of the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: To prove one chamber was in the north, the גמרא begins quoting a משנה: there were six chambers in the עזרה, three north and three south.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was in the north, as we learned in a משנה: There were six chambers in the courtyard, three in the north and three in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving רב פפא's claim about the northern chamber by quoting a משנה. This step sets up a long quotation that runs through the following steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not complete yet. The quoted משנה first lists all six chambers, and the key line about the כהן גדול's chamber comes later, in אבא שאול's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The Temple courtyard
Six chambers

steps.confusionAlert: This quote is from מסכת מדות, not from our משנה in יומא. Everything through the end of this passage is part of that quotation.

phrases.english: One was in the north, as we learned in a mishna:
There were six chambers in the courtyard,
three in the north and three in the south.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source proof for the northern chamber in רב פפא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that one of the כהן גדול's chambers was in the north
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מדות listing the six chambers of the עזרה

steps.title: The three southern chambers and their uses
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה lists the southern chambers (salt, hides, rinsers) and their functions, including the כהן גדול's immersion room on the roof of the hides chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: The southern ones were the Salt Chamber, the Hides Chamber, and the Rinsers' Chamber. In the Salt Chamber they placed salt for the offerings. In the Hides Chamber they salted the hides of קדשים, and on its roof was an immersion room for the כהן גדול on יום כיפור. In the Rinsers' Chamber they rinsed the innards of קדשים, and from there a spiral staircase went up to the roof of the Hides Chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה continues by naming the three southern chambers and explaining what each was used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part is background within the quotation. It does not yet speak about the כהן גדול's northern chamber. Notably, the כהן גדול's immersion room for יום כיפור was on the roof of the לשכת הפרוה, reached by the staircase from the לשכת המדיחין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Salt Chamber, where salt for the קרבנות was stored
The Hides Chamber, where the hides of קדשים were salted
The Rinsers' Chamber, where innards were washed
An immersion room
A spiral staircase

phrases.english: Those in the south: the Chamber of the Salt,
the Chamber of the Parva, the Chamber of the Rinsers.

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַמֶּלַח — שֶׁשָּׁם הָיוּ נוֹתְנִין מֶלַח לַקׇּרְבָּן,
phrases.english: The Chamber of the Salt: where they would place salt for the offering,

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַפַּרְוָה — שֶׁשָּׁם הָיוּ מוֹלְחִין עוֹרוֹת קָדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: the Chamber of the Parva: where they would salt the hides of consecrated animals.
And on its roof was a place of immersion
for the High Priest on Yom Kippur.

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַמְּדִיחִין — שָׁם הָיוּ מְדִיחִין קִרְבֵי קָדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: The Chamber of the Rinsers: there they would rinse the innards of consecrated animals.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשָּׁם מְסִיבָּה עוֹלֶה לְגַג בֵּית הַפַּרְוָה.
phrases.english: And from there a spiral staircase ascended to the roof of the Parva chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with the details of the southern chambers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The southern chambers were salt, hides (with the כהן גדול's יום כיפור immersion room on its roof), and rinsers.

steps.title: The three northern chambers; the wood chamber's use was forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The northern chambers were wood, exile, and hewn stone. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he forgot what the wood chamber was used for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The three in the north were the Wood Chamber, the Exile Chamber, and the Chamber of Hewn Stone. About the Wood Chamber, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said: I forgot what it was used for.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה turns to the northern side and lists its three chambers. Its author admits he does not remember what the first one was used for, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is where the proof for רב פפא will come from. The open question about the לשכת העץ gives אבא שאול the opening to identify it as the כהן גדול's chamber.

keyTerms.meaning: The Wood Chamber
The Exile Chamber
The Chamber of Hewn Stone
I forgot

phrases.english: The three in the north:

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הָעֵץ, לִשְׁכַּת הַגּוֹלָה, לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית.
phrases.english: the Chamber of the Wood, the Chamber of the Exile, the Chamber of Hewn Stone.

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הָעֵץ, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: The Chamber of the Wood: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov said:
I forgot what it was used for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves within the quoted משנה from the southern chambers to the northern ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The northern chambers were wood, exile, and hewn stone. The use of the wood chamber was forgotten by רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: אבא שאול: the כהן גדול's chamber was in the north
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול identifies the northern chamber as the כהן גדול's chamber, standing behind the other two and sharing one roof with them. This proves רב פפא's northern chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: The chamber of the כהן גדול was behind the two of them, and the roof of all three was level.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the proof. אבא שאול places the כהן גדול's chamber on the northern side, which shows that one of his two chambers was in the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול fills in what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forgot: the northern chamber served the כהן גדול. It stood behind the לשכת הגולה and the לשכת הגזית, and all three were joined under one level roof. This establishes the northern half of רב פפא's statement. The southern half is proven in steps 9-11.

keyTerms.meaning: Behind the two of them
Roof
Level, equal

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's northern chamber is proven from אבא שאול's statement in the משנה in מדות. Which of his two named chambers stood there is not settled here; steps 12-17 take up that question.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הָיְתָה אֲחוֹרֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן,
phrases.english: The chamber of the High Priest was behind the two of them,
and the roof of all three was level.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: לִשְׁכַּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הָיְתָה אֲחוֹרֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question about the wood chamber and supplies the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: The northern chamber of the כהן גדול in רב פפא's statement
steps.raayaSupportSource: אבא שאול in the משנה in מדות: the כהן גדול's chamber was on the northern side, behind the other two

steps.title: The Exile Chamber and its well
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: the לשכת הגולה held a well with a wheel over it, which supplied water to the whole עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Exile Chamber there was the Exile Well, with a wheel placed over it, and from there they supplied water to the entire courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה to the end of its list. This part is background and is not needed for the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chamber was named after the well dug by those returning from exile. The wheel was used to draw water for washing throughout the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exile Well, dug by the returnees from בבל
A wheel for drawing water
Supply

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַגּוֹלָה — שָׁם הָיָה בּוֹר הַגּוֹלָה,
phrases.english: The Chamber of the Exile: there was the well of the Exile,
and the wheel was placed over it,
and from there they supplied water to the entire courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁכַּת הַגּוֹלָה — שָׁם הָיָה בּוֹר הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation, explaining the second northern chamber.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לשכת הגולה contained the well that supplied water to the whole עזרה.

steps.title: The Chamber of Hewn Stone: the סנהדרין judges the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: In the לשכת הגזית the סנהדרין judged the כהנים. A disqualified כהן left dressed in black, and a fit כהן dressed in white and joined the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Chamber of Hewn Stone the סנהדרין of Israel sat and judged the כהנים. One found to have a disqualification would put on black, wrap himself in black, and go out on his way. One found without a disqualification would put on white, wrap himself in white, and go in and serve with his fellow כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה ends by describing the third northern chamber, where the סנהדרין checked whether כהנים were fit to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court examined each כהן for a פסול, such as a bodily blemish or a flaw in his lineage. Black clothing showed sorrow at being turned away, and white clothing showed joy at being approved. This is background in the quotation, not part of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court of 71 judges
A disqualification, such as a blemish or flawed lineage
Wraps himself
Black garments / white garments

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית — שָׁם הָיְתָה סַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Chamber of Hewn Stone: there the Sanhedrin of Israel
would sit and judge the priests,
and one in whom a disqualification was found
would wear black and wrap himself in black
and go out and go on his way.
And one in whom no disqualification was found
would wear white and wrap himself in white
and enter and serve with his brothers the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית — שָׁם הָיְתָה סַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quotation with the third northern chamber.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the לשכת הגזית the סנהדרין examined the כהנים. Disqualified ones left in black, and fit ones served in white.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how carefully the מקדש guarded the fitness of those who served, and the process was public and emotional.

steps.title: Proof for the southern chamber begins with the gates of the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets out to prove the כהן גדול had a chamber in the south. It quotes a משנה listing the seven gates of the עזרה, starting with the southern gates and the eastern gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was also one chamber in the south, as we learned in a משנה: There were seven gates in the עזרה, three in the north, three in the south and one in the east. The southern gates were the Gate of Kindling, then the Gate of the Offering, then שער המים. The eastern gate was שער ניקנור. It had two chambers, one on its right and one on its left. One was the chamber of פנחס the Dresser, and one was the chamber of the makers of the חביתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof that the כהן גדול had a chamber in the south. Right now it is only quoting the source that tells us where the gates were. The punchline comes later in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that matters for the proof is that שער המים is one of the southern gates. The rest of the משנה, like the eastern gate and its chambers, is quoted because the גמרא quotes the משנה in full. Keep שער המים in mind, because the ברייתא in step 11 will connect it to the כהן גדול's chamber.

keyTerms.meaning: The Water Gate, one of the three southern gates of the עזרה. This is the key detail for the proof.
The שער ניקנור, the single eastern gate of the עזרה
פנחס the Dresser, who was in charge of the priestly garments
The daily griddle-cake offering brought by the כהן גדול
'As we learned in a משנה.' This introduces a quote from a משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in all the gate names. For this proof, the only detail you need is that שער המים was in the south.

phrases.english: One in the south, as we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: רב פפא said there were two chambers. We've already seen the north one, and here comes the south one.

phrases.english: Seven gates were in the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ בַּצָּפוֹן וְשָׁלֹשׁ בַּדָּרוֹם וְאֶחָד בַּמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: three in the north, three in the south, and one in the east.
Those in the south: the Gate of Kindling,
second to it, the Gate of the Offering,
third to it, the Water Gate.
phrases.notes: This is the key detail: the Water Gate is in the south.

phrases.english: The one in the east: the Nicanor Gate,
and two chambers were there,
one on its right and one on its left.
One was the chamber of Pinchas the Dresser,
and one was the chamber of the makers of the griddle-cakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 proved the northern chamber. This step opens the parallel proof for the southern chamber.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that the כהן גדול had a chamber in the south
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the seven gates of the עזרה, which places שער המים in the south

steps.title: The quoted משנה lists the northern gates
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with the three northern gates: the Gate of the Spark, with its guard post, then the Gate of the Offering, then the Gate of the House of the Hearth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The northern gates were these. First, the Gate of the Spark. It was a porch-like building with an upper story built on top. There the כהנים guarded from above and the לויים from below, and an opening led from it inward to the חיל. Second to it was the Gate of the Offering. Third to it was the Gate of בית המוקד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the gates משנה by listing the northern gates. This is background and not the core of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the full picture of the seven gates. Nothing here proves the southern chamber. The proof depends only on the southern שער המים from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The Gate of the Spark, the first northern gate
A porch-like building with a roof that is not fully closed on all sides
The rampart, an area surrounding the Temple courtyard
The House of the Hearth, where the כהנים warmed themselves and slept at night

phrases.english: Those in the north: the Gate of the Spark,
it was a portico building,
and an upper story was built on top of it,
and there priests guarded from above,
and Levites from below.
And inside of it was the rampart.
Second to it, the Gate of the Offering,
third to it, the Gate of the House of the Hearth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the same quoted משנה from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three northern gates were the Gate of the Spark, which was a guard post with an upper story, the Gate of the Offering, and the Gate of בית המוקד.

steps.title: The High Priest's first immersion was beside his chamber at the Water Gate
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the כהן גדול's first immersion on יום הכפורים was on the roof of שער המים, beside his chamber. Since שער המים is in the south, he had a chamber in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: The כהן גדול performs five immersions and ten washings of his hands and feet on that day. All of them are in the holy area, on the roof of בית הפרוה. The exception is this first one, which was in the non-holy area, on the roof of שער המים. And it was beside his chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the proof. The ברייתא places the כהן גדול's chamber beside שער המים, and step 9 showed that שער המים is in the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put the two sources together. The משנה says שער המים is in the south. The ברייתא says the first immersion was at שער המים, 'beside his chamber.' So the כהן גדול had a chamber in the south, which confirms the second half of רב פפא's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersions in a מקוה
Here this means washing the hands and feet from the כיור, not betrothal
The לשכת הפרוה (hides chamber), inside the holy area. The other immersions were done on its roof.
In the non-holy area, outside the sanctified courtyard
'And it was taught in a ברייתא.' This introduces a ברייתא.

steps.whatToRemember: משנה: שער המים is in the south. ברייתא: the first immersion was at שער המים, beside the כהן גדול's chamber. Together they prove the כהן גדול had a southern chamber.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word קדושין means washing the hands and feet before the service. It has nothing to do with marriage.

phrases.english: And it was taught: five immersions and ten sanctifications

phrases.aramaic: טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: the High Priest immerses and sanctifies on that day,
phrases.notes: 'That day' means יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: and all of them are in the sacred area,
on the roof of the Hall of the Parva,
except for this one, which was in the non-sacred area,
phrases.notes: This is the first immersion of the day, which every כהן does before entering the עזרה.

phrases.english: on top of the Water Gate,
and it was beside his chamber.
phrases.notes: This is the proof: his chamber was next to a southern gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supplies the second half of the proof that began in step 9 by linking שער המים to the כהן גדול's chamber.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן גדול had a chamber in the south
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the five immersions, which places the first immersion at שער המים 'beside his chamber'
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the proof of רב פפא's claim that the כהן גדול had two chambers, one in the north and one in the south.

steps.title: Which named chamber was in the south? Probably the Parhedrin chamber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it does not know which of the two chambers, לשכת פרהדרין or לשכת בית אבטינס, was in the north and which was in the south. It concludes that it is more reasonable that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we do not know whether לשכת פרהדרין was in the north and לשכת בית אבטינס in the south, or לשכת בית אבטינס was in the north and לשכת פרהדרין in the south. It is reasonable that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both locations are proven, the גמרא tries to match the two named chambers to north and south. It is unsure, but it leans toward לשכת פרהדרין being the southern one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs showed where the chambers were, but not which name goes with which place. The גמרא leans toward placing לשכת פרהדרין in the south. The next step gives the reason: this layout keeps the כהן גדול's daily walking to a minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרהדרין chamber, where the כהן גדול stayed during the seven days before יום הכפורים
The chamber of בית אבטינס, the family that prepared the incense
'I do not know.' This states that the matter is uncertain.
'And it is reasonable.' This introduces a conclusion based on logic, not on a direct source.

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול had two chambers, one north and one south. The גמרא is unsure which was which. It suggests that לשכת פרהדרין was the southern one, but this suggestion is rejected in steps 15-17.

phrases.english: But we do not know
whether the Parhedrin chamber was in the north
and the Chamber of the House of Avtinas in the south,
or the Chamber of the House of Avtinas in the north
and the Parhedrin chamber in the south.
And it is reasonable
that the Parhedrin chamber was in the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי לִשְׁכַּת פַּרְהֶדְרִין בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With both locations now proven, this step tries to identify which named chamber was in each place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול had chambers in both the north and the south. The גמרא tentatively suggests that the southern one was לשכת פרהדרין, but steps 15-17 reject the reasoning behind this suggestion.

steps.title: Why the south makes sense: the short daily route
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains its reasoning. If לשכת פרהדרין is in the south, the כהן גדול's daily routine needs very little back-and-forth walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He gets up early, relieves himself, and immerses in the south next to his chamber. He goes to the north and practices taking handfuls of incense. He comes to the בית המקדש and does the service all day. Toward evening they sprinkle purifying water on him. Then he goes back to the south, immerses, and rests in his chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it decided in Step 12 that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south. It walks through the כהן גדול's daily schedule to show that this layout gives him an easy route.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from Step 11 that he immersed in the south. If his own chamber is also in the south, he wakes up, immerses, and at night immerses again and goes to sleep, all in the same area. He only goes north once, to practice חפינה in לשכת בית אבטינס.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Literally 'covers his legs.' A polite way of saying he relieves himself.
Immersion in a מקוה
Taking a double handful of incense (קטורת). The כהן גדול does this on יום הכפורים, and it needs practice.
Toward evening
They sprinkle (purifying water) on him

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'south' here comes from Step 11. The ברייתא said he immersed on the roof of שער המים next to his chamber, and that gate is in the south. So every time he immerses, he is in the south.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He's asking why Step 12 comes out the way it does.

phrases.aramaic: מַקְדֵּים קָאֵי וּמֵיסֵךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו וְטָבֵיל,
phrases.english: He gets up early, relieves himself, and immerses,
phrases.notes: He immerses in the south, next to his chamber.

phrases.english: and goes to the north and practices taking handfuls,
phrases.notes: In the north is לשכת בית אבטינס, where the incense was prepared.

phrases.english: and comes to the Temple
and performs the service the whole day.
Toward evening they sprinkle (purifying water) on him,
and then he goes back to the south, immerses, and rests.
phrases.notes: He immerses and sleeps in the same place, so there is no extra trip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind Step 12's conclusion that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south.
steps.raayaObject: That לשכת פרהדרין was in the south
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: this layout makes the כהן גדול's daily route as short as possible

steps.title: The other option: a tiring route if the chamber was in the north
steps.stepSummary: If לשכת פרהדרין were in the north, the כהן גדול would have to walk south to immerse and then walk all the way back north to sleep. Would we really burden him that much?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say לשכת פרהדרין was in the north: he gets up early and relieves himself, goes to the south and immerses, practices taking handfuls, comes to the בית המקדש and serves all day. Toward evening they sprinkle on him. He goes back to the south and immerses, and then he has to walk back to the north to rest. Do we really make him go to so much trouble?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its argument by comparing the other layout. With the chamber in the north, the כהן גדול has to keep walking back and forth, and the גמרא asks whether we would really make him do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he always immerses in the south, a northern chamber means a long walk south every morning. Every night he walks south to immerse and then all the way back north to sleep. The question 'do we burden him this much?' assumes we would want to spare him, so the southern layout seems more reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you say
The כהן גדול's private chamber, where he stayed during the seven days before יום הכפורים
We make (him) go to trouble; we burden (him)
This much; to this extent

phrases.english: For if you say the Chamber of Parhedrin was in the north,
he gets up early and relieves himself,
and goes to the south and immerses,
phrases.notes: First long trip, from his chamber in the north to the immersion place in the south.

phrases.english: and practices taking handfuls,
phrases.notes: In this layout, לשכת בית אבטינס is in the south.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָתֵי לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְעָבֵיד עֲבוֹדָה כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: and comes to the Temple and performs the service the whole day.
Toward evening they sprinkle on him,
and he goes back to the south and immerses,
and then he has to go back to the north to rest.
phrases.notes: Second long trip, from the south back to the north.

phrases.english: Do we really burden him this much?
phrases.notes: The answer is obviously 'no,' and that supports putting things in the south.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the hard northern route with the easy southern route from Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That לשכת פרהדרין was in the south
steps.raayaSupportSource: The assumption that we would not put so much walking on the כהן גדול

steps.title: Rejection: we do want to burden him, so a צדוקי will quit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the assumption that we would avoid burdening him. On the contrary, extra trouble is useful, because a צדוקי כהן גדול might give up and step down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? We burden him even more, so that if he is a צדוקי, he will quit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 14. It says there is a good reason to make the כהן גדול work harder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 assumed that burdening the כהן גדול is something to avoid. The גמרא answers that the burden has a purpose. A צדוקי, who does not truly accept the חכמים, would not put up with all this effort and would step down. That would be a good result. So the 'he walks less' argument no longer proves anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
More
A צדוקי, a member of the group that rejected the תורה שבעל פה
He will withdraw, quit

phrases.english: Why not?
We burden him even more,
so that if he is a Sadducee, he will quit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 14's assumption that we would avoid burdening the כהן גדול.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes we want to spare him effort, but the extra effort is intentional and useful.

steps.title: Second reason for the burden: so he does not become arrogant
steps.stepSummary: Another reason to keep him busy: so that even a good כהן גדול does not become proud of his high position.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or alternatively: so that he will not become arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason for making the כהן גדול work hard. This reason applies even when he is a good, God-fearing person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason only helps if the כהן גדול is a צדוקי. This reason covers every כהן גדול. If he is busy rushing from place to place, he has no time to feel important about his high position.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively
So that he will not become arrogant

phrases.english: Or alternatively,
so that he will not become arrogant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, שֶׁלֹּא תָּזוּחַ דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, broader reason why burdening him is useful.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Extra effort is wanted even for a good כהן גדול, to keep him humble.

steps.title: Proof that the burden is intentional: two separate chambers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that the trouble was planned on purpose. If not, they would have built his two chambers next to each other, or given him only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, let them build both chambers next to each other, or else one chamber should be enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection with a proof. The way the chambers were set up shows that the extra effort was deliberate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal were to save the כהן גדול effort, there would be no reason to give him two chambers on opposite sides of the courtyard. They could be side by side, or he could have just one. Since they were set far apart, the trouble was on purpose. So the 'less walking' argument fails, and we still cannot tell which chamber was in the south.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say this
Next to each other
One should be enough for him

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to prove that לשכת פרהדרין was in the south fails. The burden on the כהן גדול was intentional, either to push out a צדוקי or to keep him humble. The two chambers being far apart shows this.

phrases.english: For if you do not say this (that the burden is intentional),
let them make both chambers next to each other,
or else one chamber should be enough for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in Steps 15-16 that the burden on him was deliberate.
steps.raayaObject: That the burden on the כהן גדול was intentional
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that he had two separate chambers far apart, not one chamber or two side by side

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the elders address the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of a line from the משנה, where the elders speak to the כהן גדול. This sets up a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they said to him: My master, כהן גדול,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה, where the זקני בית דין tell the כהן גדול that he is their agent. This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to ask a question based on this wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line in the משנה is: 'We are שלוחי בית דין, and you are our שליח and the שליח of בית דין.' The word וכו׳ tells us to remember the rest of the line. The key part is that the כהן גדול is called 'our agent'.

keyTerms.meaning: My master. A respectful way to address someone.
Etc. The rest of the quote is understood from the משנה.
An agent of the court. The משנה uses this phrase for the כהן גדול.

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first words are quoted here. The important part, 'you are our שליח,' is in the hidden 'וכו׳'. That is the phrase the next step builds on.

phrases.english: And they said to him:
phrases.notes: The זקני בית דין speak to the כהן גדול before יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: My master, High Priest, etc.
phrases.notes: The quote continues in the משנה: 'we are agents of the court, and you are our agent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the discussion of the לשכות and their placement, and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elders tell the כהן גדול that he serves as their agent and the agent of בית דין.

steps.title: Does this משנה refute רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's wording, which calls the כהן גדול 'our agent', may be a refutation of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible challenge. The משנה calls the כהן גדול 'our agent,' and that seems to go against a known view of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לימא means 'shall we say.' It shows this is only a suggested challenge, and the גמרא may answer it later. The conflict is about whom the כהן works for: the people, or ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say. It introduces a suggestion that is often rejected later.
Let it be. Shall it be.
A strong refutation of an אמורא's view from an earlier source.

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whose agent a כהן is affects how we understand the whole עבודה, and it matters for laws of שליחות.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
phrases.notes: A suggested challenge, not yet final.

phrases.english: of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: The אמורא whose view seems to be challenged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's wording, quoted in step 18, to challenge an אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's view that כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה calls the כהן גדול 'our agent.' That implies כהנים represent the people, which goes against רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא's view: כהנים are agents of ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: the כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא, agents of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: These כהנים are agents of the Merciful One.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the statement that the משנה seemed to contradict. רב הונא says the כהנים act for ה׳, not for us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, a כהן does the עבודה because ה׳ commanded him and sent him. He is not acting for the people who brought the קרבן. This is exactly what clashes with 'you are our שליח' in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: These כהנים, meaning the ones who offer the קרבנות.
Agents of the Merciful One, meaning ה׳.
They are.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: As Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
These priests are agents of the Merciful One,
phrases.notes: They represent ה׳, not the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the view that step 19 said might be refuted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים doing the עבודה are agents of ה׳, not agents of the people.

steps.title: רב הונא begins his proof: what if they were our agents?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא starts to prove his view by asking us to imagine that the כהנים were our agents. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you say they are our agents...
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts a proof by imagining the opposite view. This is a setup line, and the sentence finishes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof that works by showing the opposite view leads to a problem. רב הונא will show that if the כהנים were 'our agents,' something would not make sense. That problem will push us back to his view that they are שלוחי דרחמנא.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you say. It introduces the opposite idea in order to reject it.
Ours.
Agents of.

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. Do not stop at 'they are our agents' and think רב הונא agrees with it. He is bringing up this idea only to reject it.

phrases.english: For if you say they are our agents,
phrases.notes: The opposite view is raised so that it can be disproved. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the reasoning behind רב הונא's statement in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That כהנים are שלוחי דרחמנא, not agents of the people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: showing that the opposite view, that they are our agents, leads to a problem. The problem is spelled out on the next amud.
